question: pass 146 left open: why did the all-48 diffusion run compare 57.32 % of the diffusion mass when 98.735 % is carriable?
answer: ANSWERED. The run did not include diffusion_conditioning -- 26 tensors, ZERO of them uncarried, holding 41.415 % of the diffusion module's gradient mass.
the_arithmetic_closes_exactly: carried diffusion tensors = 761 - 188 = 573; the run compared 547; 573 - 547 = 26
diffusion_conditioning has exactly 26 tensors and exactly 0 uncarried
98.735 % carriable - 41.415 % (diffusion_conditioning) = 57.320 %, which is the run's own share_of_diffusion_sq_norm = 0.5732
so the 26 tensors the run omitted ARE diffusion_conditioning, to three digits

what_it_is_worth.cross_check: 51.14 + 36.95 = 88.09, which equals the measured carried-diffusion share of the model (88.082 %) plus rounding -- the two routes agree

why_this_is_the_best_available_lever: it is 26 tensors. They are CARRIED -- our port builds them, 0 uncarried -- and the finite-difference run already validated the reference on two of them (diffusion_conditioning.transition_s.1.layer_norm.bias at 5.088e-03 and transition_s.0.layer_norm.weight at 1.501e-05). Including them roughly DOUBLES the campaign's measured gradient coverage, from 51.14 % to about 88.08 % of the model, without touching the port.
what_is_NOT_claimed: that they will PASS. Coverage is not parity -- including them could easily make the model-scope median worse, and given they are the most concentrated block in the section that already fails at 1.6588e-01 median, that is the likely outcome. The claim is that they are measurable and currently unmeasured, which is a different and prior thing.
history: the campaign recorded at pass 59-ish that diffusion_conditioning's 26 tensors carry '33.61 % of the diffusion magnitude' and sit outside our DiffusionModule boundary. That figure was computed on the 0.5.0 model; on the correct 0.4.3 basis it is 41.415 %. The observation was right and was never followed up.
